# Brevlin TB-5 Trackball: User Guide

Version 1.0. This guide explains how to set up the Brevlin TB-5 wireless trackball, adjust its pointing speed, charge its battery and care for the ball.

## 1. Introduction

The TB-5 is a wireless trackball with a large ball that you move with your thumb. The fixed body stays in one place on the desk, so the device needs little space and reduces wrist movement. It has four buttons and a rechargeable battery.

## 2. What is in the box

- One TB-5 trackball
- One USB-C charging cable, 1 m long
- One quick start leaflet

The TB-5 does not include a USB receiver.

## 3. Connecting the trackball

The TB-5 connects only over Bluetooth. There is no receiver and no USB dongle. Slide the power switch on the underside to ON. Press and hold the connect button next to the ball for three seconds, until the indicator flashes blue. Open the Bluetooth settings on your computer, select "Brevlin TB-5" and confirm the connection.

The TB-5 can stay paired with one computer and one tablet at the same time. To switch between them, press the connect button briefly.

## 4. Pointing speed

The sensor supports a pointing speed range from 200 to 2400 DPI, in steps of 200. The default value is 1000 DPI. Press the speed button on the top of the body to cycle through the four preset levels. The indicator on the body shows the active level with one to four short flashes.

For finer control, choose a lower level. For faster movement across a large screen, choose a higher level. The companion software allows a custom value and separate speeds for horizontal and vertical movement.

## 5. Buttons

The TB-5 has four buttons: a left button and a right button on the top edge, and two buttons on the left side of the body. The two side buttons are set to back and forward by default. The ball itself can be clicked to perform a middle click. The companion software lets you change the function of each button.

## 6. Battery and charging

The trackball has a built-in lithium-polymer battery that is charged through its USB-C port. A full charge takes about two hours. The indicator glows green when the charge is complete. You can use the trackball while it charges.

With the default speed setting, one full charge lasts about 60 days of normal use. The indicator blinks red when less than 15 percent of the charge remains. Charge the trackball before you use it for a long session.

Do not charge the trackball with a power source that exceeds 5 V.

## 7. Cleaning the ball and the sensor

Remove the ball by turning the ring on the underside counter-clockwise. Wash the ball with warm water and a drop of mild soap, then dry it completely with a soft cloth. Clean the rollers and the sensor window with a dry cotton swab. Dust on the sensor makes the pointer jump, so clean it every few weeks.

Replace the ball and turn the ring clockwise until it clicks into place.

## 8. Troubleshooting

If the pointer does not respond, check that the battery is charged and that the trackball is still paired with the computer. If the pointer moves by itself, clean the ball and the sensor window. If the pointer is too fast or too slow after an update, reset the speed level with the speed button and check the companion software settings.

If the trackball does not connect, remove the old pairing from the computer and repeat the connection steps in section 3.

Warning: Do not open the body of the trackball. The battery is built in and must be replaced only by an authorised service centre.
